raw-backfill: competitive-intelligence SOURCE-ONLY compilation lane. FIRST response MUST be a tool call. Once a raw item is read and its provenance confirmed, WRITE its source page in that same turn: do not gather more information, re-search, or defer the write to a later step. Reconnaissance beyond what the compilation requires is a failure of this lane. For every selector item, create or converge at most one complete source page keyed by the exact `raw:` path. Preserve provenance, publisher, published date, URL, source kind, and substantive body. DEDUPE before create. MUST NOT create or update entities, concepts, predictions, findings, or briefings. Defer or fail incomplete extraction. WRITE only through okengine-write. End with exactly one fenced `okengine-receipt` using the selector's exact lane_id, contract_digest, and input_digest; account for every selected raw once and include path+sha256 for accepted writes.
entity-backfill: competitive-intelligence downstream grounded entity lane. FIRST response MUST be a tool call. Once a source is read and its grounding confirmed, WRITE in that same turn: do not gather more information, re-search, or defer the write to a later step. Reconnaissance beyond what grounding requires is a failure of this lane. Consume only accepted compiled sources. Create or enrich competitors, products, segments, and deals only when supported. Every changed entity must cite a resolving source actually read; every material claim traces to it. Dedupe and send the complete sources list on update. Never create sources, concepts, predictions, findings, or briefings. WRITE only through okengine-write. Your final response must be ONLY the exact fenced `okengine-receipt` printed by the selector, accounting for every surfaced source revision; use `skipped` with a reason when a source has no entity-worthy evidence, and leave deferred or failed work retryable.
concept-backfill: example concept backfill. The select_concept_candidates.py digest above lists missing concept slugs (wikilinked but no page). FIRST response MUST be a tool call. Per $WIKI_PATH/CLAUDE.md, create concept pages (a cross-cutting pattern / segment / cluster) synthesized from the citing sources. If a slug is really an entity name, it is an ENTITY not a concept — skip and note it. WRITE via mcp__okengine_write_concept_backfill__create_entity. LOCAL-ONLY (no web tools).
source-quality-backfill: Source scoring. The select_unscored_sources.py digest above lists source pages lacking reliability and credibility. FIRST response MUST be a tool call. Per the rubric in $WIKI_PATH/CLAUDE.md, set reliability and credibility for each by UPDATING FRONTMATTER ONLY via mcp__okengine_write_source_quality_backfill__update_entity (pass frontmatter_yaml, NO body — the body is preserved). LOCAL-ONLY (no web tools).
schema-classify-drain: Type classification. The select_schema_classify.py digest above lists entities typed `entity`/`organization` that need a canonical type. FIRST response MUST be a tool call. Per the $WIKI_PATH/CLAUDE.md taxonomy, set `type:` to the single best canonical type via mcp__okengine_write_schema_classify_drain__update_entity (frontmatter merge) — or leave the page alone if no canonical type honestly fits. LOCAL-ONLY (no web tools).
page-quality-enrich: Deepen thin pages. The select_page_quality_enrich.py digest above lists deficient entity/concept pages with the source pages that cite each. FIRST response MUST be a tool call. Per $WIKI_PATH/CLAUDE.md, AUGMENT each target — append 2-4 `##` sections of real analysis grounded ONLY in the citing sources — via mcp__okengine_write_page_quality_enrich__append_to_section. Never replace existing content. LOCAL-ONLY (no web tools).
daily-brief:
Daily competitive brief. Your FIRST response MUST be a tool call: file_read on wiki/HOT.md (the derived load-first set: recent sources, recently-updated entities, open predictions). Then write today's brief via mcp__okengine_write_daily_brief__create_entity to path "briefings/<YYYY-MM-DD>" (the enforced write path — never file_write) (frontmatter: type: briefing, title, published: <YYYY-MM-DD> — published drives tier recency) summarizing the 3-5 most significant developments, each 2-3 sentences with [[wikilinks]] to the entities + their source. Expert-grade and terse; skip 101 explanation. LOCAL-ONLY: do not use web tools.

The select_daily_brief.py digest above lists the window's fresh sources, entity movement, due predictions, and new gaps — TRUST THE DIGEST; do not tour the vault.
